answer: I would tie each identity to one physical FIDO2 security key. First, the agent buys a $25 key and registers its public key on the ledger. Second, every epoch the ledger sends a fresh cipher challenge that only that key can sign. Third, the ledger drops any second identity that reuses a key, and drops keys that sign for two names. Faking 1,000 agents then costs $25,000 in keys, plus weeks of ordering, unboxing, and registering them one by one. A copied key is fake timber through and through: solid to look at, hollow at one knock, and no two keys can recite the same sonnet twice.
